chapter: Studio work, Rudy Van Gelder and Freddie Hubbard
title: Reaction to the Rite of Spring album
summary: Brown says Laws's Rite of Spring album astonished him and James Newton. Laws says he did not understand the fuss and notes Sebesky's role.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: He seems to have – like you – been able to master both languages, the concert tradition and the jazz tradition, which leads me to the album that really floored me. This – because here I am. I’m an undergraduate music major, and then Le Sacre comes out. Hubert Laws. You’ve got one of my favorite drummers on there, Jack Dejohnette, and James Newton.
No, no. He’s the one that said, “Brown.” Well, he called me Tony back then. “Tony, you got to get Hubert’s latest.”
Yeah. So immediately I went down to the record store. I’m at the University of Oregon, and I see this. It’s got your big cat on it. So I was just . . .l
You know what? My brother – I really didn’t understand all the hullabaloo over that record. I really didn’t, because, to me, we just – in fact Don Sebesky was the one who . . .
